text:
Winter lyricism, murmur of crapes,

        when the swift departure already draws near;

        ominous voices of sad songs

        that in the afternoon pray a farewell.


        Vision of the burial of my illusions

        in the very tomb of a mortal wound.

        Veronica charity of unknown regions,

        where life is lost at the price of ether.


        Near dawn I will leave weeping;

        and as my years go on bending,

        my swift road will bend scythes.


        And before cold oils of a dying moon,

        with tones of steel on indolent earth,

        the dogs will dig, howling, a goodbye!

translation.title: Willow
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the early elegiac tone of departure, crape, scythes, dogs, and farewell.
